purpose: Independent evidence-based review of BMX in the current isolated ReSkate build
scale: 0 to 10; half-point increments; 9.5 is near release quality with no reproducible material fault in the covered scenarios
current_score_status: Unrated until current-build gameplay footage covers every category. Test counts, source review, telemetry and older footage cannot substitute for viewing the current game.

acceptance.aggregate: Minimum score across judges and categories; averaging cannot hide a weak category
acceptance.disagreement: Preserve both scores and cited timestamps, reproduce the disputed scenario, repair or obtain additional evidence; never lower the target to close a disagreement
acceptance.human_controller_gate: The owner must confirm steering, braking, hopping, trick timing and recovery feel good with their physical controller. An AI footage review cannot certify tactile feel or input latency by itself.
acceptance.iteration: Freeze source and runtime hashes, record all planned trials including failures, judge independently, fix named failures, then recapture changed categories plus a continuous regression ride. Preserve prior reports.

score_anchors.meaning: Missing or routinely unusable; severe visible faults dominate
Core behavior exists but frequent disruptive faults prevent credible riding
Usable prototype; recognizable BMX with repeatable rough transitions or limitations
Strong and consistent; small but noticeable defects remain
Natural, predictable and coherent throughout the required trials; only negligible cosmetic imperfections remain
No meaningful issue observed across complete evidence; this is bounded by the tested conditions, not a guarantee of perfection

hard_failures: Process crash, unresponsive game, indefinite stuck state, or unintended reset during a judged trial
Bike or rider passes through the map, explodes, teleports, or remains inverted without a justified crash response
Bike vanishes during an ordinary fall or the game silently changes equipment to skateboard
Input mapping contradicts the requested left-stick handlebars/steering, right-stick rear-wheel tricks, or changes Skate Dpad mappings
Recovery leaves sticky input, rider control attached to a remote bike, invisible equipment, or motion continuing after release
hard_failure_policy: Any hard failure fails the build and caps each directly affected category at 4 until reproduced, repaired and re-recorded. Record unrelated category scores separately; do not manufacture a total pass.

categories.name: Riding and steering
judge: Steering direction and response
Smooth acceleration, braking and coasting
Predictable low- and high-speed balance
Coherent lean, wheel rotation and rider response
No visible jumpiness or artificial slow motion
scenarios: S01: 30 seconds on flat ground: start, coast, brake to rest, restart; three trials
S02: left/right slalom at low and higher speed, a full turn each direction, steering release to center; three trials
S03: low curb and uneven terrain approach at two speeds, then stop; three trials
categories.9_5_requirement: Every trial is controllable and visually continuous with correctly directed steering, stable straight riding, smooth braking and no repeated unintended bail. Physical-controller feel remains a separate owner gate.

categories.name: Ramps and landings
judge: Natural ramp entry and exit
Momentum retained without snapping or hovering
Wheel-first contact, compression and recovery
Reasonable acceptance of aligned landings
Clear distinction between a recoverable landing and a crash
scenarios: S04: ride a shallow ramp up and down at two speeds, no jump input; three trials
S05: bunny-hop a flat gap and land with aligned wheels; three trials
S06: ledge or stairs drop including the previously reported stair-edge landing, aligned and slightly off-axis approaches; three trials each
categories.9_5_requirement: Aligned landings remain stable and flow into riding. Minor contact-edge changes do not command abrupt sideways lean. Invalid impacts produce a coherent fall rather than tunneling, snapping or instant equipment replacement.

categories.name: Tricks and controls
judge: Trick recognizable from full-speed animation
Requested stick/button mapping
Release and catch timing
Combinations and interruption behavior
Landing completion consistent with the visible trick
scenarios: S07: hop, manual and nose manual; three attempts each
S08: barspin both directions and tailwhip both directions; three attempts each
S09: 180/360, one hand release, one foot release, tuck and extended body move; three attempts each
S10: two-trick combo, early release/interruption and incomplete catch landing; three trials each
categories.catalog_coverage: Every trick claimed implemented needs at least one clear current-build clip for identity/release/catch and one successful landing; representatives alone cannot certify the entire catalog. Keep an explicit tested, failed and untested trick list.
categories.9_5_requirement: Viewed tricks are distinct, physically coherent and responsive, with no body discontinuity or false success on incomplete catches. The full claimed catalog must be covered before this category can pass.

categories.name: Rider movement and bike attachment
judge: Natural torso, hip, elbow, knee and wrist shape
Hands on grips and feet on pedals while held
Pedaling, preload, hop, landing compression and lean
Intentional limb releases only
No clipping, detached grips or uncontrolled bone stretching
scenarios: S11: stationary and slow ride viewed from front, side, rear and three-quarter angles
S12: pedal, brake, steer, preload, hop and compress on landing at full speed
S13: close view of barspin/tailwhip release/catch and extended body move, followed by normal riding
categories.9_5_requirement: The rider reads as riding a bike throughout; no persistent deep crouch, elbows hanging beneath the grips, sharply bent wrists or obvious sliding contacts. Close views and ordinary gameplay views both remain coherent.

categories.name: Falls, collisions and recovery
judge: Impact-appropriate separation and native fall animation
Bike remains visible and collides with the world
No rider envelope pulling the separated bike
Readable settle and recovery
Reliable intentional remount without instant re-crash
scenarios: S14: deliberate low-speed side impact and high-speed frontal impact; three trials each
S15: sideways and inverted failed landings; three trials each
S16: let bike/rider settle, walk to bike, pick up/remount and ride away; three trials
S17: pause/focus change during recovery, then resume; two trials
categories.9_5_requirement: The rider falls naturally, bike and rider remain physically coherent, and recovery works repeatedly without disappearance, map clipping, unintended skateboard equip, uncontrolled motion, stale state or a remount crash loop.

categories.name: Bike, skateboard, mounting and carrying
judge: Clear intentional equipment switch
Mount and dismount continuity
Carry and set-down placement
Control ownership and retained Skate Dpad mappings
No ghost equipment or leftover bike force
scenarios: S18: bike to skateboard to bike, then skate and perform a native skateboard action; five complete cycles
S19: get off, walk away/back, mount and ride; three cycles
S20: pick up, carry while walking/turning, stop, set down and remount on flat and gently sloped ground; three cycles each
S21: switch after a fall and after carrying; two cycles each
categories.9_5_requirement: Each intentional action has a clear, smooth visual result and reliable controls; no unexpected board, floating bike, disappearing rider, abrupt pose snap, continued off-bike motor force or remount rejection on valid ground.

evidence_manifest_required: Run ID, UTC start/end, source manifest SHA256 and runtime DLL SHA256
Isolated executable path and SHA256, map/spawn/route, bike model manifest SHA256, profile, test mode and control mapping
Clip SHA256, byte size, codec, dimensions, duration, frame count, nominal and average frame rate, first/last timestamps, monotonic PTS and decode errors
Recording type: live renderer or native replay; replay requires proof custom bike/rider state matches live gameplay
Video-to-telemetry synchronization marker and uncertainty; preserve real-time and simulation-time measurements
Every scenario/trial and exact clip time range; retain failures, exclusions and recording interruptions
Physical controller versus synthetic input; full-speed original versus explicitly labeled slow-motion diagnostic
Judge ID, independent unshared initial report, category score, timestamped observations, confidence and coverage gaps
recording_requirements: Current frozen build; no use of old footage as evidence for new fixes
Continuous ordinary third-person gameplay at normal speed, preferably 60 frames per second, with input annotations tied to telemetry
No selective removal of bad trials; archive complete originals and index useful segments
Include close side/front views for anatomy and contacts in addition to the default riding view
Do not claim elapsed simulation time is wall-clock performance; frame pacing and encoder slowdown must be reported
Do not run heavy reverse engineering or builds during evidence recording
Unit/native telemetry tests supplement footage and catch ownership regressions; they never earn visual gameplay scores
